description: ChullaSolution is a team of Software Engineering students from ESPOCH, Ecuador, passionate about technology, innovation, and space exploration. We combine programming, creativity, problem-solving, and teamwork to explore scientific challenges. Our goal is to develop an original, functional, and meaningful solution using NASA's open data during the 2026 Space Apps Challenge.
summary: Killawasi is a free, bilingual mission trainer for children ages 7–12. Players join Timmy, an astronaut vicuña, to build and run a lunar outpost while balancing energy, water, oxygen, crew life, and radiation shielding. Solar panels generate power during the lunar day; a rover travels to a crater to collect ice and return it for processing into water and oxygen. Players maintain the habitat and repair its shield when a solar-particle alert approaches. Cadet mode guides ages 7–9, while Engineer mode adds harder planning for ages 10–12. Each short mission connects an action to a science card based on public NASA resources. The game distinguishes real science references from simplified gameplay values and is playable in a browser or offline on Windows.
details: Killawasi makes systems engineering tangible through short, interactive lunar-outpost missions for ages 7–12. A bilingual EN/ES tutorial supports two age bands: Cadet (7–9) and Engineer (10–12). Players manage solar energy, crew life support, robot battery, and shielding; travel to craters for ice; process it into water and oxygen; and respond to solar-particle alerts. The lunar day/night cycle is accelerated for play; resource levels, storm timing, and costs are gameplay abstractions, not NASA forecasts. NASA references inform the science cards and concepts, including LCROSS lunar ice, LRO/Diviner, OSDR RadLab and CCMC DONKI radiation and space-weather, ISS ECLSS water and oxygen recovery, and lunar robotics. The game is built with Godot Engine 4.7.2 and has browser and offline Windows builds. AI assistance included Codex and Gemini/Antigravity for portions of coding, debugging, research, writing, and translation; image_gen produced seven activity illustrations, and synthetic text-to-speech was used for the trailer narration. Team members reviewed and tested AI-assisted outputs; AI-generated images are visibly marked. The project uses no NASA logos or mission identifiers.
